item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is narrowly preferable because its retry change is limited to seekable bodies, while A eagerly buffers nearly every reader passed through RawClient. Neither is merge-ready: both violate the explicit requirement that Upload delegate to FilesService.Add.","reasons":["Both add the required Upload signature, use multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", validate inputs, and produce a replayable multipart request.","Both duplicate Add's option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling Add, directly violating the frozen contract and creating two implementations to maintain.","B preserves forward-only streaming behavior and limits replay support to io.ReadSeeker bodies; A's io.ReadAll applies broadly to arbitrary RawClient, Add, and Update reader bodies whenever WithNoRetry is absent.","B's retry test uses an os.File and verifies byte-for-byte equality across attempts, closely matching the reported streamed-content failure. A has better validation of request options and uniquely includes the required source-reader-error test."],"risks_a":["RawClient now eagerly reads every unrecognized io.Reader into memory even when the configured policy or HTTP method would not actually retry, risking excessive memory use, blocking on pipes, and broad behavioral changes outside file uploads.","The RawClient change also alters Add and Update behavior despite the contract's scope restrictions; WithNoRetry produces different body ownership and streaming semantics.","Upload bypasses Add and duplicates its request and response logic."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses Add and duplicates its request and response logic.","GetBody returns the same mutable io.ReadSeeker after rewinding it, rather than an independent reader as GetBody conventionally promises; this is fragile if body copies ever overlap.","RawClient seeks to the end and changes close ownership for every seekable body even when retries are disabled, so previously usable custom ReadSeekers can now fail or behave differently; Add and Update semantics are also changed beyond the requested convenience path. B also omits the contract-required source-reader-error test."]}
